context: A married couple talks about household saving
purpose: Teach: まじめ/貧乏/ときどき/ついつい/おまけ/パンツ/ふえ/やってくる

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: あなた、最近どんどん出費がふえて、本当に困ってるのよ。
lines.en: Honey, our expenses keep growing lately, and I'm really worried.
lines.style: Worried wife raising a serious household concern gently

lines.speaker: ryosuke_dad
lines.jp: うん、わかってる。会社の帰りに、ついついコンビニで買っちゃうんだよなあ。
lines.en: Yeah, I know. On the way home from work, I just can't help buying things at the convenience store.
lines.style: Sheepish husband admitting his bad spending habit

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: ときどきならいいけど、毎日でしょ?このままじゃうちは貧乏になっちゃうわ。
lines.en: Once in a while is fine, but it's every day, isn't it? At this rate we'll end up poor.
lines.style: Mildly scolding wife pressing the point firmly

lines.speaker: ryosuke_dad
lines.jp: 大げさだなあ。でも確かに、おまけ付きのお菓子とか、つい手が伸びちゃうんだ。
lines.en: You're exaggerating. But it's true, snacks with little freebies — I just reach for them.
lines.style: Defensive husband half-joking half-confessing his weakness

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: それに、あなたのパンツや靴下、もう穴だらけなのに新しいの買わないし。
lines.en: And your underwear and socks are full of holes, but you won't buy new ones.
lines.style: Practical wife pointing out a contradiction with affection

lines.speaker: ryosuke_dad
lines.jp: あはは、それは節約してるつもりなんだよ。
lines.en: Haha, I thought I was being frugal there.
lines.style: Husband laughing off the embarrassing observation lightly

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: ねえ、来月から家計簿、まじめにつけましょうよ。子供の学費もやってくるんだから。
lines.en: Hey, starting next month let's seriously keep a household budget. The kids' tuition is coming up too.
lines.style: Determined wife proposing a concrete plan forward

lines.speaker: ryosuke_dad
lines.jp: わかった、わかった。じゃあ俺もコンビニ通いはやめるよ。
lines.en: Okay, okay. Then I'll stop my convenience store habit too.
lines.style: Husband finally relenting with a tone of cooperation
